question: how do I get credit for my internship? I need to register for it but dont know where to start
answer:
Start with the Cahill Career Development Center. Its career advisor starts the intake process and checks eligibility; the Center assists with registration procedures. [1,4]

After you’re accepted for a co-op internship:
1. Select and meet with a co-op faculty advisor to determine learning objectives and academic assignment. [1]
2. Request a co-op Experience on Handshake: http://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/. [1,2]
3. Meet with your career advisor and receive “Registration Permission” from the Career Center. [1]
4. Complete the appropriate form with Academic Advisement if you select Pass/Fail. International students on a J1 or other visa must get authorization from the international advisor and fill out the appropriate paperwork. [1]
5. Register through “Self Service” on “My Ramapo” to add the co-op course. Registration authorization only gives permission to take the course. [1]

The experience must be a learning experience applying classroom knowledge, with transferable skills, defined dates and job description, learning objectives related to your academic/career goals, professional supervision and routine feedback, and employer resources supporting learning. [3] The co-op Experience Request has student, employer, and faculty-advisor parts; a Learning Agreement must be approved by your faculty advisor, career advisor, and employment supervisor. [6,8] Students must attend orientation and reflection sessions. [8]

Credit: the Career Center page lists 2 credits for at least 120 hours and 4 credits for at least 240 hours within the semester, based on start date; co-op is available fall, spring, and summer only. [2] The catalog says each successfully completed co-op course is 4 credits. The pages differ on credit options. [8] Up to 8 credits may count toward graduation; additional co-op credits do not count toward graduation. [4,8]

Contact Cahill Career Development Center: careercenter@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7444 (Main Office, C-209) or (201) 684-7675 (ASB Office, ASB-513). [1]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/get-started/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/get-started/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/employer/) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#cooperative-education-program)

question: do transfer students need to take all the gen ed / Intellectual Inquiry requirements again or do some get waived?
answer:
No—not necessarily. Transfer students may transfer in or be waived from some or all General Education requirements under the transfer-credit and waiver policies. [3]

If you transfer with at least 48 credits but without a completed A.A. or A.S., you are waived from some requirements. The listed waived keystone courses are First Year Seminar, Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Social Science Inquiry, and Studies in the Arts and Humanities. You must still complete Critical Reading and Writing 102, Quantitative Reasoning, Scientific Reasoning, and one course from each of two distribution categories at Ramapo: Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society. Advisement will identify applicable waivers and remaining requirements. [1][2]

If you complete an A.A. or A.S. at a New Jersey community college, General Education requirements are waived after Ramapo receives your final official transcript showing the conferred degree. A.A.S. graduates do not get a full waiver; courses are evaluated individually. [8]

Generally, only transfer credits accepted in your semester of matriculation are considered for possible General Education waivers. [4] The pages describe General Education waivers, but don’t specifically explain whether “Intellectual Inquiry” is a separate requirement. [1][3]

For your individual waivers, contact the Office of the Provost at provost@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7330. [1] For transfer-credit questions, contact Admissions at admissions@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7300. [8]

question: can i appeal my financial aid if my family's income changed this year? how
answer:
The Office of Financial Aid says that if your family’s circumstances have changed, email or call to discuss your situation and the possibility of a re-evaluation of your financial aid award. It does not say this requires an appeal form. [2]

Contact: finaid@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7549. In-person appointments are available Monday through Friday, 8:30am–4:30pm; appointments can be made by email or through the website chat. [2]

The FAFSA is based on prior-year taxes. [3] Income is one factor considered in aid eligibility. [6]

question: my roommate keeps having his girlfriend sleep over like 5 nights a week. is there a guest policy and who do i talk to about it
answer:
Yes. Housing & Residence Life says guests may not move from host to host to stay on campus more than three (3) nights. Residents are responsible for their guests, and roommates should discuss guest expectations and tell the host about concerns. [1,3] Roommates have the right to sleep without unnecessary disturbances and to host guests only as long as guest policies are followed and others’ rights are respected. [8]
Contact your Resident Assistant to facilitate a roommate/suitemate/apartment contract if you want to opt out of automatic guest registration. If the contract is violated, staff in the hall/area office must receive a formal complaint before they can act; a complaint may mean all residents lose guest privileges until a contract is developed. [1,3]
Housing & Residence Life: reslife@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7461. [1,3]

Sources: [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/)

question: how do i get a work study job on campus? i have it in my aid package but idk where to apply
answer:
The On-Campus Employment for Students office says to register on Handshake (ramapo.joinhandshake.com) to view openings, search with keyword “RCNJ,” and follow the application instructions on each posting; apply directly to the hiring unit and contact its listed supervisor. [1][5][6] Priority for Student Assistant positions goes to students awarded Federal Work-Study as part of their aid package. [6] If offered a job and you accept, you and the supervisor sign an employment form; return the required New hire packet, W-4 Form and I-9 Form to the Student Assistant Program Office, Room D-119. [1]
The office lists questions about Federal Work-Study for Financial Aid: finaid@ramapo.edu. [6] On-Campus Employment for Students: sap@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7654, Room D-119. [1]
